chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His saying, 'Or two others from among you,' he said, 'If a man is in a town where there is no Muslim, the testimony of a non-Muslim is valid regarding the will/testament.'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of a non-Muslim valid for witnessing a Muslim's will?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific legal exception (rukhsah) where the testimony of a non-Muslim (ahl al-kitab) is valid for witnessing a will when no Muslims are available in the locality. This ruling highlights the pragmatic flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in ensuring the preservation of property rights even in minority contexts, relying on the reliability of the non-Muslim witness in the absence of Muslim alternatives.
